back: A force between surfaces in contact that opposes their relative motion and produces heating.
Friction on an object moving through a fluid (liquid or gas); in air it is air resistance.

front: How does drag change with speed?
Give three useful effects of friction.
back: Walking without slipping, braking, tyres gripping the road (also holding nails, striking matches).
Wear of parts, heating that wastes energy, extra fuel needed.
Lubrication, ball bearings, smooth surfaces, streamlining, air cushions.

front: Why does a car reach a top speed?
back: Air resistance grows with speed until it balances the driving force: zero resultant force.
Reduces drag by letting the fluid flow smoothly past the object.
